audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 against a 53.83% win rate over 2244 games is defensible: Irelia wins levels 1-5 outright, level 6 is Zed's, and the lane returns to her on items — the difficulty rating reflects how lethal the single level 6 window is, not the average.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3] and late credited Irelia's Defiant Dance with tenacity, and the level 6 spike text described Death Mark's payload vaguely.
audit.why: Defiant Dance reduces physical damage during the charge; it grants no tenacity and cleanses nothing. Death Mark repeats a portion of the damage Zed dealt to the target while marked, after 3 seconds.
audit.corrected: Both rewritten around the real mechanic: Defiant Dance held for the three marked seconds shrinks what the mark copies, because Zed's damage is physical.

audit.whatIsWrong: Death Mark's untargetable dash through your commit was never stated, and mid described the mark as a 'damage-over-time application'.
audit.why: The untargetability is why a spent combo evaporates, and the mark is a repeat of damage dealt, not a tick — the two require opposite responses.
audit.corrected: Untargetability written into enemyWin and phases[4].why; the repeat mechanic written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d, mid and late.
sources: enemyKit R untargetable flag and text

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Death Mark 120s at rank 1 with its 3-second mark; Living Shadow 20s at rank 1; Razor Shuriken at 75 energy.

audit.whatIsWrong: CROSS-LAYER DISAGREEMENT on six of seven rows, and the two layers were offset by one: full read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Zed/Skill/Skill while content read Irelia x5, Zed, Irelia.
audit.why: Every content why places Zed's peak at level 6 (row index 4) — whys[4], spikes[1] and mid all say so — which matches the full layer's phases[4].side of Zed and not the packet chart's row 5. The prose is the tiebreaker the chart rule asks for.
audit.corrected: Rows aligned to: 0-3 Irelia, 4 Zed, 5 Skill, 6 Irelia. phases[0..3].side and phases[6].side moved on the full layer, win[4] and win[5] moved on the content layer, and every phases[N].why rewritten to argue its row.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Bodies did not match their titles ('W the burst, stun the exit', 'Chase resets past your own wave').
audit.corrected: Rewritten to Defiant Dance during the mark, and to the 650-range Living Shadow swap.

edits.before: Q the low minions and keep the blade moving — your level 1 reset dance already out-trades careless mages.
edits.after: Q the low minions and keep the blade moving — Razor Shuriken is 75 energy at rank 1 and he cannot spam it.

edits.before: W joins: the channel shreds incoming damage — hold it for his trade spell, not his autos.
edits.after: W joins: Defiant Dance cuts physical damage, and every point of Zed's kit is physical.

edits.before: E completes the engine: the stun into stacked-passive autos is half a health bar at 3. Mid lane rarely budgets for it.
edits.after: E completes the engine: stun into four-stack autos, and Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1 — his one way out of it.

edits.before: Reset-dance the wave into his face: four stacks, E-stun, Q the kill threat. The lane is a minion-count quiz.
edits.after: Reset-dance the wave into his face: with Living Shadow spent on the wave he has nothing to swap out with.

edits.before: Vanguard's Edge online — the all-in caps with a wall of disengage-proof marks. Dive with the wave as your fuel.
edits.after: Death Mark makes him untargetable mid-commit and repeats his damage after 3 seconds — the one level he owns.

edits.before: First item spike: stacked trades delete mages and your sustain mocks their poke math.
edits.after: First item: whoever spends first loses — his shadow swap against your E stun.

edits.before: Late Irelia surfs the fight: Q-reset through their line, stun the carry pair, and shred whoever peels.
edits.after: Late your stacked on-hit trades outlast a Zed who must survive 3 seconds inside your whole team.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. It governs your forward steps. - W Defiant Dance spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Death Mark (R) is 120s at rank 1 and the mark repeats a portion of his damage after 3 seconds — Defiant Dance during those 3 seconds cuts the physical damage it copies. - Living Shadow (W) is 20s at rank 1: that is his only escape.

edits.after: Living Shadow is a 650-range swap home — chase him past your minions and you dash into an empty screen.

edits.after: Zed wins by going untargetable through your commit, swapping out on Living Shadow, and cashing the mark 3 seconds later.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the swap: Living Shadow is 20s at rank 1, and without it he has no exit from your stun.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Zed's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, drain his energy: force trades that make him spend Razor Shuriken at 75 energy, then step in while he is empty.

edits.before: Your Ultimate (Vanguard's Edge) and W tenacity let you shrug off his death-mark burst in extended fights, and your all-in speed beats his kite pattern once he's forced to commit shadows early.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge walls his exit and Defiant Dance cuts the physical damage Death Mark copies, so extended fights favour you once he has spent Living Shadow and committed early.

edits.before: You beat Zed clean from level 1 through 5 because your Q dash closes the gap on his immobile pre-6 kit and your E slow denies the kite pattern he relies on with W. Trade into him whenever his shadow is on cooldown, since without it he has no way to disengage your all-in. Watch his energy bar; if he's spamming Q to poke, punish immediately since he can't afford to keep pace with your sustained damage. Your level 3 all-in is close to unanswerable if he's already used W to clear a wave.
edits.after: You beat Zed clean from level 1 through 5 because Bladesurge closes the gap on a kit whose only reposition is a 20-second Living Shadow, and Flawless Duet stuns him out of the swap. Trade into him whenever his shadow is on cooldown, since without it he has no way to disengage your all-in. Watch his energy bar; if he's spamming Q to poke, punish immediately since he can't afford to keep pace with your sustained damage. Your level 3 all-in is close to unanswerable if he's already used W to clear a wave.

edits.before: Level 6 is Zed's clear high point: Death Mark plus a pre-placed shadow gives him a full burst combo that threatens to kill you from near-full HP before you can react, and your W block doesn't stop the mark's damage-over-time application. Play cautiously around this level, hold Q for repositioning rather than aggression, and let jungle or a support-side gank cover the all-in window. From 7 onward your itemization curve reasserts control since your stun-reset chain punishes his shadow cooldown gaps, so return to proactive trading once his ult is confirmed spent.
edits.after: Level 6 is Zed's clear high point: Death Mark plus a pre-placed shadow gives him a full burst combo that threatens to kill you from near-full HP, and the mark repeats a portion of the damage he lands rather than ticking on its own. Hold Defiant Dance for the three marked seconds so the copy is smaller, hold Bladesurge for repositioning rather than aggression, and let jungle or a support-side gank cover the all-in window. From 7 onward your stun-reset chain punishes the 20-second Living Shadow gap, so return to proactive trading once his ultimate is confirmed spent.

edits.before: With Trinity Force or Black Cleaver online you out-trade his shadow-kite pattern decisively, since your dash-stun sequence closes distance faster than he can reset with W and your damage output overwhelms his mark-and-run plan. In teamfights your Ultimate lets you dive his backline and survive the retaliation better than he can survive yours, especially with W's tenacity clearing any slows from his shuriken follow-up. Play for extended skirmishes rather than isolated burst trades late, since that format neutralizes his all-in-and-reset identity.
edits.after: With your first items online you out-trade his shadow-kite pattern decisively, since your dash-stun sequence closes distance faster than the 20-second Living Shadow comes back and your damage overwhelms his mark-and-run plan. In teamfights Vanguard's Edge walls off the swap he wants to leave on, and Defiant Dance during the three marked seconds shrinks the damage Death Mark copies back onto you. Play for extended skirmishes rather than isolated burst trades late, since that format neutralizes his all-in-and-reset identity.

notes: The two layers were offset by one row: the full layer put Zed's win at index 4 (Level 6) while the packet chart and win[] put it at index 5 (First item). Every piece of prose in the matchup — whys[4], spikes[1], mid — places his peak at level 6, so the content column was moved to the full layer's placement rather than the reverse. Defiant Dance was credited with tenacity in two content fields; it has none, and the correction reframes it as physical damage reduction held through Death Mark's three seconds, which is what actually shrinks the mark's copied damage.
